what_its_for: Ospemifene is used to treat moderate to severe painful intercourse (dyspareunia) and vaginal dryness caused by menopause. It works by acting like estrogen in certain parts of your body, helping to keep vaginal tissues moist and healthy.
how_to_take: Take ospemifene by mouth as a tablet, once a day WITH food. Taking it with a meal helps your body absorb the medicine better and may reduce side effects. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose is one 60 mg tablet taken by mouth once daily with food. Do not take more than one tablet per day unless your doctor tells you to. Your doctor will decide how long you should take this medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is still the same day and you can take it with food. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose at your usual time. Do NOT take two tablets to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store ospemifene at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about medicine take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking while taking ospemifene, as smoking increases the risk of serious blood clots and stroke. Do not take ospemifene if you are also using estrogen products (pills, patches, creams) unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Avoid prolonged bed rest or long periods of not moving (such as on long flights), as this can increase blood clot risk. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines you take, especially certain antifungal medicines (like fluconazole or rifampin), as they can affect how ospemifene works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: sudden chest pain or tightness, sudden severe headache, vision changes, sudden shortness of breath, coughing up blood, pain or swelling in your leg (especially the calf), sudden dizziness or weakness on one side of your body, or unusual vaginal bleeding. Also call your doctor if you develop breast lumps, yellow skin or eyes (jaundice), or skin rashes. These could be signs of serious side effects including blood clots, stroke, or heart attack.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in vaginal dryness and comfort during intercourse within a few weeks, but the full benefit of ospemifene typically takes about 12 weeks (3 months) of regular use. Keep taking it as directed even if you don't feel a difference right away. If you don't notice improvement after 3 months, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Ospemifene is ONLY for women who have gone through menopause and should NOT be used by women who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or who could become pregnant — it may harm an unborn baby. It is not approved for use in men or children. Women with a history of breast cancer, blood clots, stroke, heart attack, or uterine cancer should discuss the risks carefully with their doctor before using this medicine. Women with liver problems may need special monitoring or may not be able to take this medicine safely.
